question: By the time we reached the station, the train ___.

question: Which sentence is correct?
a: By next March, Meera has taught here for ten years.
b: By next March, Meera will have taught here for ten years.
c: By next March, Meera will teach here for ten years.

question: Each of the boys ___ a prize.
why: Each is singular, so it takes has.

question: She drank ___ water and felt better.

question: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ aware of the change.
why: With neither...nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject, students, which is plural.

question: He has ___ friends in the new city, so he often feels lonely.
why: Few means hardly any and carries a negative sense; a few would mean some.

question: The number of stray dogs in our colony ___ risen, while a number of residents ___ complained.

question: Bread and butter ___ my usual breakfast.

question: He said, "I am tired." He said that he ___ tired.

question: She said to me, "Close the door." She ___ me to close the door.
why: A command is reported with told or asked plus to.

question: Rohan said, "I will meet you tomorrow." Rohan said that he would meet me ___.

question: The teacher asked, "Have you finished the exercise?" The teacher asked whether I ___ the exercise.
why: A yes-no question is reported with whether or if, and the present perfect becomes the past perfect.

question: She said, "I have been waiting here since morning." She said that she ___ there since morning.

question: "Let's go for a walk," said Kabir. Which is the correct report?

question: Look! The baby ___ at the picture.
why: Look! shows the action is happening now, so we use the present continuous.

question: We ___ our cousins in Pune last summer.

question: You ___ cross the road when the signal is red. It is dangerous.
why: Must not shows a strong prohibition.

question: She ___ swim when she was five years old.
why: Could shows ability in the past.

question: The sun ___ in the east.
why: A general truth takes the simple present.

question: By the time Dad came home, we ___ dinner.
why: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect.

question: I ___ in this school since 2022.
why: Since with a starting point takes the present perfect.

question: This time next week, we ___ on a beach in Goa.
why: This time next week points to an action in progress in the future, so we use the future continuous.

question: She ___ be at home; her car is outside.
why: Must shows a strong guess based on evidence.

question: Ravi ___ the whole book yet.
why: Yet with a negative sentence takes the present perfect, and the main verb is the past participle.

question: My sister ___ for the exam since morning. She is tired.
why: Since morning with an action that is still going on takes the present perfect continuous.

question: If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic.
why: In a real future condition the if-clause takes the simple present.

question: If I ___ you, I would apologise to her.
why: An imaginary present situation takes were in the if-clause.

question: If he had left earlier, he ___ the train.
why: A past unreal condition takes would have plus the past participle.

question: She said she ___ the project by Friday.
why: After a past verb, will changes to would.

question: Which sentence is correct?
a: She has been wait for two hours.
b: She has been waiting for two hours.
c: She is waiting since two hours.
d: She waits for two hours now.

question: The teacher, along with her students, ___ going to the museum.
why: Along with does not make the subject plural. The subject is the teacher.

question: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.
why: Names of subjects ending in s are singular.

question: There ___ two apples left in the basket.
why: The real subject apples is plural, so use are.

question: He is ___ honest boy.
why: Honest starts with a vowel sound, so we use an.

question: I have ___ money left; I cannot buy the book.
why: Little means almost none and goes with uncountable nouns.

question: ___ sun rises in the east.
why: There is only one sun, so we use the.

question: Either Priya or her brothers ___ coming.

question: Each of the players ___ given a medal.
why: Each is singular.

question: Ten kilometres ___ a long distance to walk.

question: The news of the floods ___ shocking.
why: News is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb.

question: She gave me ___ advice about my career.
why: Advice is uncountable, so a and an cannot be used.

question: ___ of the students were absent, so the class was cancelled.
why: Of the students needs a plural idea. Most fits and makes sense with the cancelled class.

question: The principal as well as the teachers ___ present at the function.
why: As well as does not change the subject. The subject is the principal.

question: Two-thirds of the pizza ___ eaten, and two-thirds of the guests ___ gone.
why: With a fraction the verb agrees with the noun after of: pizza is singular and guests is plural.

question: Tom said, "I can drive." Tom said that he ___ drive.

question: He said to me, "Open the window." He ___ me to open the window.

question: He said, "I live here." He said that he lived ___.

question: Father said, "I am going to Delhi today." Father said that he was going to Delhi ___.

question: The teacher said, "Do not make noise." The teacher told us ___ noise.

question: Ria said, "I have finished my work." Ria said that she ___ her work.
why: The present perfect changes to the past perfect.

question: "Where do you live?" asked Sam. Sam asked me where ___.
why: A reported question uses statement order and shifts to the past.

question: Mohit said to Sunil, "Will you help me?" Mohit asked Sunil ___.
why: A yes-no question uses if with statement order and will changes to would.

question: The mother said to her son, "Please sit down." The mother ___ her son to sit down.

question: She said, "What a beautiful garden!" She ___ that it was a beautiful garden.
why: An exclamation is reported with exclaimed.

question: He said, "Let us go to the market." He ___ going to the market.
why: Let us shows a suggestion.

question: The doctor said to the patient, "Don't eat oily food." The doctor advised the patient ___ oily food.
why: Advice is reported with advised plus not to plus the base verb.

question: Rani said, "I saw him yesterday." Rani said that she had seen him ___.
why: Yesterday becomes the day before and saw becomes had seen.

question: He said to me, "Why did you not come to the party last night?" He asked me why I ___ to the party the night before.
why: Past simple changes to past perfect and last night becomes the night before.

question: The teacher said, "The earth moves around the sun." The teacher said that the earth ___ around the sun.
why: A universal truth stays in the simple present.

question: Neha said to Kavya, "May God bless you!" Neha ___ that God might bless her.
why: A blessing or wish is reported with prayed or wished, and may changes to might.

a: The captain said them don't be afraid.
b: The captain told them do not be afraid.
c: The captain told them to don't be afraid.

question: Which is the active form of "The cake was baked by Mother."?

question: In "She was late because the bus broke down", the clause "because the bus broke down" is an

question: The letter ___ before you arrive.

question: Which is the passive of "Someone has stolen my bicycle."?

question: Which sentence has an adjective clause?

question: Which sentence CANNOT be changed into the passive voice?

question: Join "Work hard. You will succeed." using an adverb clause of condition.
a: Because you work hard, you will succeed.

Last month, the panchayat decided to stop the service because few adults borrowed books. But when Raju bhaiya showed that fifty-two children had borrowed books that month, the panchayat reconsidered. The van still comes on Thursdays, and now it carries picture books in Marathi as well.

The last sentence suggests that the service
b: is changing to suit the village
why: Adding picture books in Marathi shows it adapts to local needs.

question:
Passage: Honeybees communicate through dance. When a worker bee finds flowers rich in nectar, she returns to the hive and performs a "waggle dance". The angle of her dance shows the direction of the flowers relative to the sun, and the length of the waggle shows how far they are. Other workers watch closely and then fly out to the spot. Scientists once believed only humans could pass on such detailed directions.

The words "once believed" suggest that scientists now
c: know animals can also give detailed directions
why: Once believed points to an old idea that has since changed.

Instead, she erased the board, wrote one sentence, "Be curious, even when no one is marking you," and quietly picked up her bag. For a moment nobody moved. Then Farah began to clap, and the whole class rose.

The sentence on the board suggests that Mrs Iyer valued
